sentences.text: Researchers used genetic tools and behavioral tests on mice that drank alcohol for four weeks to measure consumption levels and signs of anxiety or depression.

Activating connections from the prelimbic cortex to the nucleus accumbens core lowered drinking and reduced anxiety and depression, while a protein analysis identified PPP1R1B as important in those cells; conversely, altering PPP1R1B in connections from the infralimbic cortex to the amygdala affected alcohol use and anxiety but did not change depression-like behaviors.
The authors conclude that different parts of the prefrontal cortex control alcohol use and emotional issues through separate pathways, noting that these findings are limited to the mouse model.
